newsitem.title: MALAWI: UNITED NATIONS TO PROVIDE LOAN GUARANTEE TO MALAWIANS.
newsitem.headline: UNITED NATIONS TO PROVIDE LOAN GUARANTEE TO MALAWIANS.

text.p: The United Nations Credit Development Fund (UNCDF) approved a $11.2 million credit guarantee scheme for Malawi's small and medium entrepreneurs, a U.N. official said on Tuesday.

U.N. Development Programme officer Allan Chimtedza told Reuters in an interview the money would be used to help Malawians gain access to capital funding, because lending institutions are reluctant to help risky groups.

"The idea was to involve commercial banks to start lending to risky groups. What we did was to provide collateral in the form of letters of credit," Chimtedza said, adding that the UNCDF would cover 75 percent of the default by beneficiaries.
Chimtedza said although a three-year programme worth $580,000 existed which winds up in June this year, the new programme, starting in July, would run for another three years.
He said the new scheme was basically a continuation of the previous one which covered water borehole rehabilitation, rural motorised transport and credit guarantee funding.
Non-Governmental Organisations would acquire the loans wholesale from commercial banks to cut down on bureaucracy.
